hypothesis: GQA-packed baseline (grid (batch,8), one program per (b,kv_head) handling its 4 query heads) reads K/V from HBM once per group; establishes correctness on all 48 workloads and a baseline geomean.
change_summary: Initial Triton kernel. Grid (batch, num_kv_heads=8). BLOCK_H=16 (4 real query rows padded/masked to 16 for tensor-core MMA), BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_D=128. Online softmax base-2 via qk_scale=sm_scale*log2e + exp2, lse=m+log2(l). q@K^T bf16 inputs/fp32 accum (no tf32); second dot p@V in fp32 with input_precision=ieee. Empty-seq guard where(l>0,...) -> out=0, lse=-inf. Page ids cast to int64 before pointer math.
reason: Baseline is correct on all 48 and already very fast (geomean 378x) because reference is a pure-python double loop. Accept as the spine. Next: c002 tries bf16 second dot (tensor-core p@V) to speed the inner loop on the larger-seq workloads (batch16 kv>12k, batch64) which show the lowest solve times relative to work; must stay 48/48 within tolerance.
notes: valid_run=True. batch1 workloads bottom out around 0.046-0.14ms regardless of seq (launch/latency bound, 8 CTAs). Largest absolute solve times: 1e15ed03 (0.169ms, kv=12942), ccdc67b6 (0.196ms, kv=20911), batch64 ~0.30-0.33ms — these are the HBM-bound cases where tuning matters. Some batch64 rel errors up to 4.6e-1 but matched_ratio gate still passes (bf16 output tail elements).

hypothesis: H2: casting p to bf16 and running the second dot p@V on tensor cores (bf16xbf16, fp32 accum) instead of fp32-ieee speeds the inner loop on the HBM/compute-bound large-seq workloads while staying 48/48 within tolerance.
change_summary: Only change vs c001: second dot. Load V as bf16 (no fp32 cast) and compute acc += tl.dot(p.to(bf16), v) on tensor cores instead of tl.dot(p,v,input_precision='ieee'). Everything else identical.
reason: Big win: geomean 378.12x -> 466.88x (+23%). batch64 nearly doubled (0.30-0.33ms -> 0.19-0.20ms; ~700-800x -> ~1170-1310x) and the large batch16 cases improved (1e15ed03 0.169->0.141ms, ccdc67b6 0.196->0.154ms). Still 48/48 pass. New spine. Absolute output error grew (abs up to 1.56e-2, rel large where reference magnitude ~0) but the matched_ratio=0.99 gate still passes on every workload, confirming bf16 p is acceptable. Next: c003 raises num_stages 2->3 to hide the paged-gather latency on the bandwidth-bound batch64/large-batch16 cases; parent=c002.
notes: valid_run=True. batch1 unchanged (latency-bound). The improvement is concentrated exactly on the HBM-bound targets identified in c001. rel error is uninformative here because many reference elements are ~0; abs error (<=1.56e-2) and matched_ratio are the meaningful gates and all pass.

hypothesis: H3: raising num_stages 2->3 pipelines the paged K/V gather (load latency of the next tile overlapped with the current tile's MMA/softmax) and improves the bandwidth-bound batch64 and large-batch16 workloads while staying 48/48.
change_summary: Only change vs c002: num_stages 2 -> 3 in the kernel launch. Kernel body, grid, tiles, dtypes all identical.
reason: Improvement: geomean 466.88x -> 489.78x (+4.9%). Concentrated again on the HBM-bound cases: the two largest batch16 (1e15ed03 0.141->0.108ms, ccdc67b6 0.154->0.128ms) and all batch64 (0.19-0.20ms -> 0.17-0.19ms; ~1170-1310x -> ~1280-1460x). batch1 slightly noisier/lower (69-84x vs 72-113x) since deeper pipeline gives no benefit on the tiny latency-bound cases and adds a little launch overhead, but net geomean clearly up. Still 48/48. New spine. Next: Phase C tile tuning -- c004 tries BLOCK_N=128 (fewer loop iterations, bigger gather bursts) on the large-seq cases; parent=c003.
notes: valid_run=True. Ref times vary run-to-run (python double loop, noisy) so per-workload speedups have wide variance in batch16/64; the solve-time deltas (ms) are the reliable signal and confirm the large-seq cases got faster. Remaining headroom: batch1 (8 CTAs, launch/latency-bound -- split-KV Phase D candidate could help) and the two biggest batch16 cases (single long sequence per kv-head across only 8 CTAs -> also split-KV territory).

hypothesis: H4: BLOCK_N 64->128 halves the loop-iteration count and issues larger paged-gather bursts, improving the bandwidth-bound large-seq workloads (batch64, big batch16) while staying 48/48.
change_summary: Only change vs c003: BLOCK_N 64 -> 128. Grid, dtypes, num_warps=4, num_stages=3 all identical.
reason: Improvement: geomean 489.78x -> 521.27x (+6.4%). Concentrated on the HBM-bound cases: batch64 0.17-0.19ms -> 0.156-0.174ms (~1280-1460x -> ~1400-1730x); the two biggest batch16 1e15ed03 0.108->0.094ms, ccdc67b6 0.128->0.100ms. batch1 essentially flat (latency-bound, one workload 233743f3 dipped to 64.5x from pipeline/launch noise on a tiny 547-token case). Still 48/48. New spine. Next: c005 sweeps num_warps (try 8) on this BLOCK_N=128 config to see if more warps help the long-seq MMA/gather throughput; parent=c004. If num_warps offers nothing, move to Phase D split-KV for batch1 and the 2 big batch16 cases.
notes: valid_run=True. BLOCK_N=128 means K/V smem per stage = 128*128*2B = 32KB each, x2 (K,V) x3 stages ~ 192KB -> near H100 smem cap but compiled/ran fine at num_warps=4. This is why a num_warps bump may or may not fit; watch for compile/smem issues in c005.

hypothesis: H5: num_warps 4->8 on the BLOCK_N=128 config gives more warps to hide gather/MMA latency and improve long-seq throughput on batch64/big-batch16 while staying 48/48.
change_summary: Only change vs c004: num_warps 4 -> 8. BLOCK_N=128, num_stages=3, dtypes, grid all identical.
reason: Regression: geomean 521.27x -> 487.61x (-6.5%) vs c004. num_warps=8 hurt the batch64 cases (max ~1440x vs c004 ~1730x; solve times 0.153-0.186ms vs c004 0.156-0.174ms -- slightly worse and noisier) and did not help batch16. With only BLOCK_H=16 effective M rows and D=128, 8 warps over-subdivide the small MMA tiles and add scheduling overhead; 4 warps is better for this shape. Reverted source to c004 (sha256 88aaa1e3... confirmed). c004 remains the spine. Next: Phase D split-KV (flash-decoding) as c006 to raise occupancy for batch1 (8 CTAs) and the 2 big batch16 single-long-seq cases (1e15ed03, ccdc67b6), which are the only remaining headroom; parent=c004.
notes: valid_run=True. Confirms num_warps=4 is the right choice for the BLOCK_H=16/D=128 tile; closes the num_warps knob. Ref times this run lower (~220ms batch64) reflecting normal run-to-run noise in the python reference; the meaningful comparison is candidate solve-time ms, which regressed for batch64.

hypothesis: H6: split-KV/flash-decoding for the low-occupancy regime (batch*8 < 64 CTAs, i.e. batch=1 -> 8 CTAs) splits each sequence into S=16 chunks over grid (batch,8,S)=128 programs + an LSE combine kernel, raising occupancy and hiding gather latency for batch1; batch>=8 keeps the c004 single-pass path so batch16/64 are unchanged.
change_summary: Added two kernels (split decode writing partial acc/m/l over S chunks, and an LSE combine kernel over grid (batch,num_qo_heads)). run() dispatches: batch*num_kv_heads<64 -> split path (S=16, BLOCK_N=64); else -> unchanged c004 single-pass (BLOCK_N=128). Single-pass kernel body identical to c004.
reason: Regression: geomean 521.27x -> 417.16x (-20%) vs c004, entirely from batch1. The split path made batch1 WORSE: ~45x (0.090-0.099ms) vs c004 ~64-90x (0.051-0.066ms). Reason: batch1 sequences are short (kv 2..547), so they are launch/latency-bound, NOT occupancy-bound; adding a second kernel launch + intermediate fp32 partial buffers (batch,32,16,128) doubles the launch/latency cost on tiny data instead of helping. The two big batch16 cases (which DO have long sequences) stayed on the fast path (batch*8=128>=64) so were unchanged -- the split heuristic never targeted them. batch16/64 identical to c004 as intended. Conclusion: split-KV is the wrong tool here; the batch1 floor (~0.05ms) is launch overhead that split-KV increases, and the long-seq cases that could benefit have enough CTAs already. Reverted source to c004 (sha256 88aaa1e3... confirmed) -- c004 stays the spine. Phase D closed.
notes: valid_run=True. Correctness of the split+combine path fully verified (batch1 all pass, including empty-ish kv=2 case abs=9.77e-4, and exact matches on kv=10/14 with abs~1e-6). The combine LSE-merge math is correct; it is purely a performance loss for this workload mix.
